completion_data.completion_summary: Wrapped and gated seven previously-invisible inventory tables across six FormalSystem/ READMEs, resolving every phantom/missing/mis-keyed row before wrapping so no hand-written description was dropped. Demonstrated coverage via 7 corrupt/restore cycles (each producing FAIL INV naming exactly the expected README, restored to an empty diff) and a full-gate run reporting ALL CHECKS PASSED.

memory_candidates.content: scripts/check-module-invariants.sh's inventory_rows() gates a subdirectory-row Lines-cell substitution on the `cols` option, not `rows`: cols=files-lines computes [file_count, total_lines] for a subdirectory row, while any other cols value (including cols=lines under rows=both) always emits a literal em-dash for that row, with no numeric substitution. When wrapping a README whose table mixes loose-file rows and subdirectory summary rows under cols=lines, expect the subdirectory rows to keep their hand-written em-dash and embedded '(N files)' prose permanently -- this is intended generator behavior, not a bug to fix.

When corrupting a single numeric cell in a markdown table for a corrupt/restore coverage demonstration, prefer a line-targeted `sed -i 'N s/old/new/'` substitution (line number from a prior grep -n) over a clever multi-command sed one-liner with address ranges and conditional branches -- the latter is easy to get subtly wrong (e.g. a loop that overruns and deletes the rest of the file) and the failure mode (massive unintended deletion) is only caught by diffing afterward, by which point recovery requires `git show HEAD:<path> > <path>` rather than a pathspec checkout (which is blocked by the destructive-git guard on a dirty shared worktree anyway).
